coaching.headline: Serath went eight kills and zero deaths, the team lost every detected fight, and two kills all game is barely a fucking pulse.
coaching.team: The team took the first Fangtooth, then lost all three detected fights and finished with two kills to the enemy's fourteen. Serath ran the game: eight kills, no deaths, the most objective damage and healing in the game, and every Steel death. The enemy took Mini Prime, the next Fangtooth, all three Seedlings and the only tower that fell. The only enemy hero to die was Riktor, twice, both times to TwinBlast.
coaching.lossReflection: The alternative was to stop handing Serath fights. The team's only kills landed on Riktor, and each was followed shortly by Serath killing TwinBlast. Treating a Riktor kill as the signal for the whole team to back off together, instead of staying for the next hit, aims to keep the trades from snowballing Serath. No plan guarantees a different result, but the current one gave Serath eight kills for zero deaths.

focus.title: Find Serath before the objective
focus.action: Before each Seedling, Fangtooth or Mini Prime, one player calls where Serath last showed. If nobody knows, the team gathers near Steel instead of walking in one at a time. Next game, count how many team deaths land on the enemy jungler.

8.4.call: Greystone killed Scarlett, Serath killed Steel and Riktor killed Crunch in a 0-3 sequence, with a River objective going to the team in the same window. The record cannot show who engaged or whether those deaths were one fight.

11.7.call: TwinBlast killed Riktor at the same moment Serath killed Crunch, then Serath killed TwinBlast and Iggy & Scorch. The allied outer tower fell in that window, after Mini Prime had already gone and shortly before the enemy Fangtooth.

13.8.call: Neon killed Iggy & Scorch and TwinBlast killed Riktor within seconds, then Serath killed TwinBlast, Crunch and Steel. The enemy took a Seedling in the same window. A Riktor kill does not pay for three deaths to the same jungler.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.matchup: Duo was Steel and TwinBlast against Riktor and Murdock. Riktor's Skewer suppresses and Shock Therapy silences; Murdock roots with Static Trap and fires Long Arm of the Law, which ignores physical armor at unlimited range. The bigger threat was Serath, the opposing jungler, who killed Steel all three times. Heaven's Fury makes Serath immune to crowd control and invulnerable during the dash, and each hero takedown drops a visage that grants Serath Heresy at no cost.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Xenia was the only completed item: health, both armors and ability haste, plus a shield on allies standing right beside Steel, with a cooldown per ally. Heavy Metal turns that armor into extra magical damage on heavy punches and Shield Bash, and Hybrid Defence adds a small slice of each armor type from bonus armor of the other type, so armor items stretch a little further on Steel. The shield only helps TwinBlast or Iggy & Scorch when Steel is close enough to touch.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.eternal: Krix adds maximum health and size, Regenerative Tissue regenerates health after a stretch without hero damage, and Cannibalism adds permanent health on takedowns. With two takedowns, Cannibalism paid little. Festering Wounds is the draft alternative to Regenerative Tissue: Steel's stuns would cut healing on the target, and Serath had the most healing in the game, giving up the out-of-combat regeneration.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.augment: Heavy Metal adds magical on-hit damage to heavy punches and Shield Bash based on total physical and magical armor, so Xenia feeds the bonus. Bulldozer is the peel-minded alternative: Bull Rush gains damage reduction on top of being Unstoppable, giving up the armor-based damage. Neither changes whether Steel is in range when Serath lands.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.crest: Sanctification shields Steel and nearby heroes for a few seconds with extra tenacity while the shield holds, raises the ward cap, adds passive gold and reduces minion gold. Against Murdock's root, Serath's slows and the brief Crushing Descent stun, the tenacity has a clear purpose. Steel placed the most wards in the game, though placement totals cannot show how often the extra slot was filled. Activations are not recorded.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.improvement: The winning core is Xenia, Dynamo and Gaia Greaves; Steel had only Xenia complete. Dynamo adds health and physical armor and makes immobilized enemies take more damage, which every Steel stun triggers. Gaia Greaves adds more physical armor against three physical damage dealers, and Hybrid Defence turns part of that into magical armor too. With one completed item, nothing in this match proves the build cost a fight; Xenia is a sound keep.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.matchup: The lane opponent was Greystone: physical damage, the Assault The Gates leap, a passive that deflects a basic attack on a cooldown and gains physical armor and regeneration as health drops, and Stone Forged Soul's stasis heal. Greystone killed Scarlett once and never died. Across the match, Serath brought the most healing in the game, and Murdock's Static Trap root and Riktor's Skewer suppress were the lockdown to respect.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.build: Tainted Blade adds physical power, health and haste, cuts healing on physical damage, and makes ability damage on a target already cut hit harder. Tainted Blade was the team's only anti-heal item, a direct answer to Greystone's regeneration and Serath's healing. Nothing in the build adds armor against Greystone, Serath and Murdock.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.eternal: Marrow heals for part of hero damage, more at low health. Blood Bank stores hero damage as charges that grant lifesteal, and Roses pays bonus gold on takedowns and boosts Marrow after hero kills. With no kills or assists, Roses paid nothing this game. Jealousy is the draft alternative to Roses: more damage as health falls, independent of takedowns, giving up the gold.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.augment: Volcaic Slam makes Empowered Cindara leave a rupture that erupts shortly after, dealing damage and slowing enemies. The slow helps stick to Greystone or hold Serath near the team. Scarlet Dawn is the alternative if First Intent's dash and shield matter more: hero hits shorten First Intent's cooldown, giving up the slow.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.crest: Liberator cleanses all debuffs and grants a short shield. Against Murdock's Static Trap root and Neon's slows and mesmerize, the cleanse has clear targets. Activations are not recorded, so whether Liberator was available in the one death to Greystone is unknown.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.improvement: The matchup flag notes no armor against three physical damage dealers. Scarlett died once, so armor is not proven necessary here. Keep Tainted Blade as the team's anti-heal. If Greystone or Serath start ending exchanges before Swan Song lands, a physical armor item in the next slot is the comparison, trading damage for staying in the fight.

64df5e4c-dd6b-4648-8f09-99bc06a06ff8.matchup: Duo was TwinBlast and Steel against Murdock and Riktor. Murdock finished with no deaths: Buckshot shreds physical armor and pushes back, Static Trap roots, and Long Arm of the Law ignores all physical armor from unlimited range. Riktor's Riplash pulls heroes and Skewer suppresses. Serath killed TwinBlast both times, each shortly after a TwinBlast kill on Riktor.
64df5e4c-dd6b-4648-8f09-99bc06a06ff8.build: Mutilator was the only completed item: physical power, haste and omnivamp, with maximum-health damage on basic attacks and a triple application when an ability hits a hero. Vaporize and Vortex Grenade hits on heroes trigger that triple application. Nothing in the build adds anti-heal or defense.
64df5e4c-dd6b-4648-8f09-99bc06a06ff8.eternal: Vermis adds maximum-health physical damage on every third consecutive basic attack on the same hero, Serration adds missing-health damage to that hit, and Melting Point adds damage only against heavily armored targets. Sub-Surface, which reduces damage from area abilities such as Serath's Heresy and Neon's Data Burst, is the draft alternative to Melting Point if surviving dives matters more than the armor bonus.
64df5e4c-dd6b-4648-8f09-99bc06a06ff8.augment: Grenadier adds a Vortex Grenade charge and refunds one on Rocket Dash, so more slows are ready while repositioning. Against Serath, an extra slow after the dash helps open distance. Amplified Burst is the alternative, adding Vaporize range for safer poke and giving up the extra grenade.
64df5e4c-dd6b-4648-8f09-99bc06a06ff8.crest: Pacifier dashes, empowers the next physical damage instance and allows a recast after a hero kill. TwinBlast deals physical damage, so the empowered hit applies, and the dash adds another escape beside Rocket Dash and Blink. Activations are not recorded, so whether the dash was available when Serath arrived is unknown.
64df5e4c-dd6b-4648-8f09-99bc06a06ff8.improvement: The winning core is Solaris, Tainted Rounds and Vanquisher. Tainted Rounds is the clearest comparison: anti-heal on basic attacks against Serath, who had the most healing in the game, plus attack speed and crit chance, trading Mutilator's omnivamp, haste and maximum-health damage. Scarlett's Tainted Blade was the only anti-heal on the team. One completed item cannot prove a build cost a fight.

f647bbff-e974-4ef9-9899-1cde1163a946.matchup: The mid opponent was Neon: Erase Vector dashes and can be recast only while Overclocked, Ghost in the Machine adds a moment of invisibility after that dash, Data Burst slows and also mesmerizes when Overclocked, and the Final Thread bomb grows with missing health. Neon took first blood on Iggy & Scorch and got one more kill on Iggy & Scorch later. Murdock got two more kills on Iggy & Scorch outside any detected fight, and Serath one.
f647bbff-e974-4ef9-9899-1cde1163a946.build: Dreambinder adds magical power and health and slows on ability damage, at a reduced rate for damage over time; Entropy adds magical power, mana and haste with extra damage on ability hits. Both suit a kit built on fire fields, turrets and oil. Neither adds defense, and Iggy & Scorch has no dash beyond Blink.
f647bbff-e974-4ef9-9899-1cde1163a946.eternal: Vesh echoes part of ability damage to heroes as damage over time, Lich adds magical lifesteal by level, and Mind Rot adds current-health damage to the echo. That fits a hero who keeps enemies standing in fire. Tithe of Death is the draft alternative to Lich, restoring mana and adding permanent haste on takedowns; with one takedown this game, Lich is the sound keep.
f647bbff-e974-4ef9-9899-1cde1163a946.augment: Turret Maniac raises the turret cap to four at lower turret health. More turrets hold more space, but each one breaks faster. Hold This! is the alternative, permanently adding explosion damage to Molotov each time the explosion hits a hero, trading turret count for ramping burst.
f647bbff-e974-4ef9-9899-1cde1163a946.crest: Epoch puts Iggy & Scorch into stasis to wait out incoming damage. Without a dash, stasis only buys time for teammates to turn on the attacker, so the crest pays most when Steel is close. Activations are not recorded, so whether Epoch was available in the deaths to Murdock and Neon is unknown.
f647bbff-e974-4ef9-9899-1cde1163a946.improvement: The winning core is Orb Of Growth, Entropy and Megacosm; Iggy & Scorch had Entropy and took Dreambinder in place of Orb Of Growth. Orb Of Growth gives up some of Dreambinder's health and the slow for mana, healing on every cast and bonus experience that evolves the item. With five deaths the sustain is the comparison, but the record cannot show which deaths a different item would have changed.

177c1537-65a7-4e57-b342-2ea4298a9092.matchup: The jungle opponent was Serath, who finished with eight kills, no deaths and the most objective damage in the game. Heaven's Fury dashes to a target while immune to crowd control and invulnerable, Chastise slows, Crushing Descent lets Ascend stun briefly, and each hero takedown drops a visage that grants Serath Heresy at no cost. Riktor killed Crunch once and Serath twice.
177c1537-65a7-4e57-b342-2ea4298a9092.build: Berserker's Axe was the only completed item: physical power, health, haste and movement speed. Blitz empowers the next basic attack with a slow after a dash or leap, and Forward Crunch's dash triggers Blitz. Nothing in the build adds armor against Serath, Murdock and Greystone.
177c1537-65a7-4e57-b342-2ea4298a9092.eternal: Lotus grants random bonuses every two minutes and on takedowns, Early Bloom grants an extra level on reaching level twelve, and Prima Donna adds damage to heroes while taking more damage from all sources. Crunch took the most damage on the team, so the downside applied to every hit, while the upside needs hero damage. Immaculate, damage reduction near full health, is the draft alternative to Prima Donna.
177c1537-65a7-4e57-b342-2ea4298a9092.augment: Lunge Crunch extends Forward Crunch, the dash that stuns, so engages and escapes start from farther away. Combo Crunch is the alternative: Cross Crunch damage grants stacking attack speed, trading reach for sustained damage.
177c1537-65a7-4e57-b342-2ea4298a9092.crest: Iceskorn Talons creates an ice sheet that gives allies on the sheet physical power and movement speed and slows enemies standing on the sheet. The crest is a group-fight tool rather than a personal escape, so the value depends on teammates fighting on the sheet. Activations are not recorded.
177c1537-65a7-4e57-b342-2ea4298a9092.improvement: The winning core is Berserker's Axe, Augmentation and Salvation; Crunch had only Berserker's Axe. Salvation adds health and tenacity, plus a shield and omnivamp when health drops low, the most direct survival comparison against Serath. The matchup flag notes no armor against three physical damage dealers. One completed item cannot show what a different second item would have changed.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Xeebs did the support paperwork: a hand in both team kills, the most wards placed in the game, the team's only ward cleared and the most damage mitigated on the team.

Serath killed Steel all three times, twice before the ten-minute mark, like a tank-shaped piñata. Heaven's Fury makes Serath immune to crowd control mid-dash, so hold Bull Rush or Shield Bash until Serath reappears on a teammate.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Cuban Noobster died once, the fewest on the team, in a game where the team died fourteen times, with farm right on the recorded Scarlett norm. Keep that discipline.
No kills, no assists and hero damage a quarter under the recorded Scarlett norm is a lantern with no flame. When Serath lands on a teammate, Swan Song goes on Serath.
64df5e4c-dd6b-4648-8f09-99bc06a06ff8: Rain_Gaup scored both team kills, both on Riktor, and died only twice, well under the recorded TwinBlast norm. In a two-kill game, the carry was the only one drawing blood.

Serath killed TwinBlast shortly after each Riktor kill, and a support kill is worth fuck all when the carry dies right after. When Serath reappears on TwinBlast, Vortex Grenade slows Serath and Rocket Dash heads toward Steel.
f647bbff-e974-4ef9-9899-1cde1163a946: Aqua led the team in hero damage, second in the whole game, and farmed above the recorded Iggy & Scorch norm. The damage rate still sat well under that norm.

Five deaths, the most in the game, is a fucking donation drive: three outside any detected fight, two to Murdock. When Murdock or Neon is missing from the map, Iggy & Scorch plays behind turrets near Steel.
177c1537-65a7-4e57-b342-2ea4298a9092: Pinkigh led the team in objective damage and healing. But no kills, no assists and the lowest hero damage in the game is a jungler bringing a pillow to a knife fight.
Serath killed Crunch twice, once in the lost teamfight shortly before the enemy Fangtooth. Once Serath is ahead, Crunch only takes a fight with Steel or Scarlett close enough to follow.

threats: Chain-CC risk (3 hard-CC abilities, ~2.5s of lockdown): Riktor Riplash (pull), Riktor Shock Therapy (silence 0.8s), Riktor Skewer (suppress 1.25s). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Dive threat on our backline: Serath. Assign peel for the carry and ward the flanks.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Crunch Right Crunch (knockup 1.25s), Iggy & Scorch Inferno (knockback). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Vortex Grenade → Vaporize pierce → Rocket Dash reposition → Ventilate ult
ourKits.winCondition: reposition with Rocket Dash and unload Ventilate from safety
ourKits.passive: abilities grant AS + a triple-shot next basic
ourKits.playWith: a frontline to create his free-fire window
ourKits.playAgainst: he's mobile but squishy — CC through the dash, then burst

ourKits.combo: Forward Crunch gap-close stun → Right Crunch knockup → empowered Left Crunch, sustain via Re-Crunch
ourKits.winCondition: all-in a squishy with the empowered combo and heal back through Re-Crunch
ourKits.passive: post-ability empowered basic that refunds cooldowns
ourKits.playWith: peel-stripping engage so he reaches the backline
ourKits.playAgainst: peel/CC him off — without resets he's stranded; anti-heal blunts Re-Crunch

ourKits.combo: Oil Spill → Molotov ignite → Flame Turret → Inferno knockback ult
ourKits.winCondition: layer fire zones on a choke/objective and burn the team
ourKits.playWith: CC that holds enemies in his fire
ourKits.playAgainst: don't fight in his zones — flank; kill the turret, dive him

ourKits.combo: Bull Rush knockback → Force Shield wall → Shield Slam knockup+stun ult, Shield Bash %hp
ourKits.winCondition: peel the carry with walls/knockups or engage with Shield Slam
ourKits.playWith: a carry he can wall for and peel
ourKits.playAgainst: his Force Shield blocks projectiles — reposition around it; bait Shield Slam

enemyKits.winCondition: trap for the root, then out-range with Shots Fired and finish with the global ult
enemyKits.passive: every 5th basic is a long-range bonus shot
enemyKits.playWith: frontline/peel to protect his low mobility
enemyKits.playAgainst: almost no escape — engage past the trap and he dies

enemyKits.winCondition: pull a target in and chain silence+suppress for a guaranteed kill
enemyKits.playWith: burst that deletes his pulled/suppressed target
enemyKits.playAgainst: respect Riplash range — stay spaced; cleanse/QSS the suppress

enemyKits.combo: Ascend dive → Heaven's Fury multi-strike → Chastise slow → Heresy form ult, resets on takedowns
enemyKits.winCondition: dive the backline and snowball Heresy resets
enemyKits.playWith: a frontline that creates her dive angle
enemyKits.playAgainst: peel the backline — deny the first kill and her resets dry up

enemyKits.winCondition: front-line aggressively and reset the fight with the stasis heal
enemyKits.playWith: a team that fights while he soaks and stasis-resets
enemyKits.playAgainst: don't waste burst into his stasis — wait it out; anti-heal cuts the ult heal
